### The five problems that matter most

1. **The safety net has holes exactly where children are most at risk.**
   - On a phone, a lone threat or sextortion demand that only Ward Lite catches is marked "unsure". It never reaches "urgent", the Coach or the report.
   - A calm result has no "this still feels wrong" path to help.
   - Ward never notices the child's own distress.
   - A child quoting abuse to ask for help is read as the bully.
2. **What reaches children is not what was tested.**
   - CI-built APKs and installers ship without ONNX Runtime, so Ward Lite silently doesn't run.
   - The APK won't install on 32-bit budget phones.
   - Every download link and the "Give Ward" QR code lead to a 404, because no release has ever been cut.
   - Saving a chat longer than about 200 messages to the vault fails silently.
3. **Some public claims run ahead of the code.**
   - "Never leaves the device" is false when a phone is paired with a family computer.
   - The report's green "Unchanged since it was saved" can be faked with one line of JavaScript.
   - "Helplines for the child's country" shows Pakistan's numbers to a child in Dubai.
   - The headline scorecard compares a model trained on the test datasets with one that never saw them.
4. **The campaign would outrun your own safeguarding rules.**
   - SAFEGUARDING.md says crisis paths must not be "turned on more widely until the professional review is done".
   - There is no reviewer, no safeguarding lead and no contact inbox.
   - The app currently tells children to post their corrections, optionally with real chat text, to a public GitHub issue.
5. **Discord server mode breaks a public promise.** SAFEGUARDING.md says Ward will never let an adult "receive alerts". Server mode alerts moderators, and it can tell a child who discloses abuse to "edit or delete" their message.

---

## 2. Fix first

| 1 | **Unconfirmed dangers on phones lose the strong help.** `analyze.ts:54-61` backs a Ward Lite-only flag only with nearby word-list hits or a distressed reply. A calm result offers "Practise spotting it". # The Android app (mobile/): the web build bundled inside a Capacitor shell, so Ward works with
# the internet off. Run by hand from the Actions tab (APK kept 14 days), or by pushing a v* tag,
# which attaches Ward-android.apk to that GitHub Release. The name never changes, so
# releases/latest/download/Ward-android.apk always points at the newest one.
#
# Signing: the keystore lives only in repository secrets (ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64,
# ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD, ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS, ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD). Without them a hand run
# builds a debug-signed APK instead (installable, but updates must be signed the same way),
# and a tag run fails.
name: Android app

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
  push:
    tags: ["v*"]

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 24
          cache: pnpm
      - uses: actions/setup-java@v4
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: 21
          cache: gradle
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      - run: pnpm --filter @ward/web build
      - run: pnpm sync
        working-directory: mobile
      - name: Keystore
        id: keystore
        env:
          KEYSTORE: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64 }}
        run: |
          if [ -n "$KEYSTORE" ]; then
            echo "$KEYSTORE" | base64 -d > "$RUNNER_TEMP/ward.p12"
            echo "path=$RUNNER_TEMP/ward.p12" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          elif [[ "$GITHUB_REF" == refs/tags/* ]]; then
            echo "::error::A release needs the signing secrets (ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64 and the rest)."
            exit 1
          else
            echo "::warning::No signing secrets, so this is a debug build."
          fi
      - name: Build
        working-directory: mobile/android
        env:
          WARD_KEYSTORE: ${{ steps.keystore.outputs.path }}
          WARD_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD }}
          WARD_KEY_ALIAS: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS }}
          WARD_KEY_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD }}
        run: |
          mkdir -p ../../release
          if [ -n "$WARD_KEYSTORE" ]; then
            ./gradlew --no-daemon assembleRelease
            cp app/build/outputs/apk/release/app-release.apk ../../release/Ward-android.apk
          else
            ./gradlew --no-daemon assembleDebug
            cp app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk ../../release/Ward-android.apk
          fi
          "$ANDROID_HOME"/build-tools/$(ls "$ANDROID_HOME"/build-tools | sort -V | tail -1)/apksigner verify --print-certs ../../release/Ward-android.apk | head -3
      # Ward Lite reads on the phone only if ONNX Runtime's wasm and the model are in the APK;
      # without them Ward quietly falls back to word lists alone.
      - name: Ward Lite is in the APK
        run: |
          unzip -l release/Ward-android.apk | awk '$1 > 0 { print $4 }' > apk-files.txt
          for f in ort/ort-wasm-simd-threaded.asyncify.wasm ort/ort-wasm-simd-threaded.asyncify.mjs models/ward-lite/ward-lite.json models/ward-lite/config.json models/ward-lite/tokenizer.json models/ward-lite/tokenizer_config.json models/ward-lite/onnx/model_quantized.onnx; do
            grep -qxF "assets/public/$f" apk-files.txt || { echo "::error::$f is missing from the APK"; exit 1; }
          done
          echo "Ward Lite: runtime and model are in the APK"
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: ward-android
          path: release/Ward-android.apk
          retention-days: 14
      # The emulator's "Give Ward to a friend" check needs a debug build: only it has the check
      # receiver. A run without signing secrets has just built one, so this costs nothing there.
      - name: Debug build for the give-a-friend check
        working-directory: mobile/android
        run: |
          [ -f app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk ] || ./gradlew --no-daemon assembleDebug
          mkdir -p ../../give && cp app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk ../../give/Ward-debug.apk
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: ward-android-debug
          path: give/Ward-debug.apk
          retention-days: 3

  # Install the APK on an emulator, open it, and keep a screenshot and the log: Ward starts,
  # shows onboarding from the bundle with no network, and doesn't crash. Then "Give Ward to a
  # friend": the copy it shares is exactly the installed APK and installs on a wiped phone.
  launch:
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          sparse-checkout: |
            packages/engine/fixtures
            mobile/ci
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: ward-android
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: ward-android-debug
      - name: Enable KVM
        run: |
          echo 'KERNEL=="kvm", GROUP="kvm", MODE="0666", OPTIONS+="static_node=kvm"' | sudo tee /etc/udev/rules.d/99-kvm4all.rules
          sudo udevadm control --reload-rules
          sudo udevadm trigger --name-match=kvm
      - uses: reactivecircus/android-emulator-runner@v2
        with:
          api-level: 34
          arch: x86_64
          target: google_apis
          emulator-options: -no-window -gpu swiftshader_indirect -no-snapshot -noaudio -no-boot-anim
          disable-animations: true
          script: |
            adb install -r Ward-android.apk
            adb shell svc wifi disable; adb shell svc data disable
            adb logcat -c
            adb shell am start -W -n org.ward.app/.MainActivity
            sleep 30
            adb exec-out screencap -p > launch.png
            adb logcat -d > logcat.txt
            adb shell pidof org.ward.app
            # Share to Ward: hand it a WhatsApp export the way WhatsApp's share sheet does.
            adb push packages/engine/fixtures/pileon-roman-urdu.txt "/data/local/tmp/WhatsApp Chat with 8B Science.txt"
            adb shell chmod 644 "'/data/local/tmp/WhatsApp Chat with 8B Science.txt'"
            adb shell am start -W -a android.intent.action.SEND -t text/plain --eu android.intent.extra.STREAM "'file:///data/local/tmp/WhatsApp Chat with 8B Science.txt'" -n org.ward.app/.MainActivity
            sleep 10
            adb exec-out screencap -p > share.png
            adb logcat -d > logcat.txt
            adb shell pidof org.ward.app
            ! grep -E "FATAL EXCEPTION.*org\.ward\.app|AndroidRuntime.*org\.ward\.app" logcat.txt
            # Give Ward to a friend: copy the installed APK as the share sheet would, check it's
            # byte for byte the same, then install that copy on a wiped "friend's phone".
            bash mobile/ci/give-check.sh Ward-debug.apk
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        if: always()
        with:
          name: ward-android-launch
          path: |
            launch.png
            share.png
            logcat.txt
            give-logcat.txt
          retention-days: 14

  release:
    if: startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')
    needs: [build, launch]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: ward-android
      - uses: softprops/action-gh-release@v2
        with:
          files: Ward-android.apk

      - run: pnpm test

# the Actions tab (kept 14 days), or by pushing a v* tag, which publishes them on the Release.
# Each packaged app is launched once (WARD_SMOKE, which also opens Ward Lite) before it's kept.

on:

jobs:

            app: release/mac-arm64/Ward.app/Contents/MacOS/Ward

          - os: macos-15-intel
            name: mac-x64
            target: --mac dmg --x64
            app: release/mac/Ward.app/Contents/MacOS/Ward
            resources: release/mac/Ward.app/Contents/Resources
          - os: windows-latest
            name: windows-x64
            target: --win nsis --x64
            app: release/win-unpacked/Ward.exe
            resources: release/win-unpacked/resources
          - os: ubuntu-latest
            name: linux-x64
            target: --linux AppImage --x64
            app: release/linux-unpacked/ward
            resources: release/linux-unpacked/resources
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 24
          cache: pnpm
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      - run: pnpm --filter @ward/web build
      - run: pnpm exec electron-builder ${{ matrix.target }} --publish never
        working-directory: desktop
        env:
          CSC_IDENTITY_AUTO_DISCOVERY: "false"
      # Ward Lite reads in the app only if ONNX Runtime's wasm and the model were packaged; the
      # launch test below then opens the model with that runtime inside the app's own page.
      - name: Ward Lite is in the app
        shell: bash
        run: |
          for f in ort/ort-wasm-simd-threaded.asyncify.wasm ort/ort-wasm-simd-threaded.asyncify.mjs models/ward-lite/ward-lite.json models/ward-lite/config.json models/ward-lite/tokenizer.json models/ward-lite/tokenizer_config.json models/ward-lite/onnx/model_quantized.onnx; do
            [ -s "${{ matrix.resources }}/web/$f" ] || { echo "::error::$f is missing from the packaged app"; exit 1; }
          done
          echo "Ward Lite: runtime and model are in the app"
      - name: Launch test
        if: runner.os != 'Linux'
        shell: bash
        run: WARD_SMOKE=1 "${{ matrix.app }}"

        if: runner.os == 'Linux'

      - name: Built-in Gemma and lab mode
        shell: bash
        run: |
          if [ "$RUNNER_OS" = Linux ]; then

            WARD_SMOKE=llama "${{ matrix.app }}" --lab
          fi
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: ward-${{ matrix.name }}
          path: |
            release/*.dmg
            release/*.exe
            release/*.AppImage
          if-no-files-found: ignore
          retention-days: 14

    if: startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write

        with:
          path: installers
          merge-multiple: true

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# "Give Ward to a friend" on the emulator (.github/workflows/android.yml, launch job).
#
# 1. Installs the debug APK (only debug builds have the check receiver) and makes the same copy
#    the share sheet gets, through GiveCheckReceiver.
# 2. Checks the copy is byte for byte the installed APK: the hash of the installed file, the
#    copy on disk, the copy read back through the FileProvider, and the plugin's own hash must
#    all match, the provider must report the APK MIME type, and the plugin's certificate
#    fingerprint must match apksigner's.
# 3. Plays the friend: pulls the copy off the "phone", uninstalls Ward, installs the copy and
#    opens it.
#
# What this can't do: a real Bluetooth or Quick Share transfer between two phones. The share
# sheet hands that to the system, which an emulator can't exercise.
#
# Usage: mobile/ci/give-check.sh Ward-debug.apk
set -euo pipefail

APK="${1:-Ward-debug.apk}"
PKG=org.ward.app
fail() { echo "::error::give-check: $*"; adb logcat -d > give-logcat.txt || true; exit 1; }

adb uninstall "$PKG" > /dev/null 2>&1 || true
adb install "$APK"
adb shell am start -W -n "$PKG/.MainActivity" > /dev/null
adb logcat -c
adb shell am broadcast -n "$PKG/.GiveCheckReceiver"

line=""
for _ in $(seq 1 60); do
  line=$(adb logcat -d -s WardGive:I | grep -m1 GIVE_CHECK || true)
  [ -n "$line" ] && break
  sleep 1
done
echo "$line"
case "$line" in *"GIVE_CHECK ok"*) ;; *) fail "the copy wasn't made" ;; esac

field() { echo "$line" | tr ' ' '\n' | tr -d '\r' | sed -n "s/^$1=//p"; }
norm() { tr -d ' :\r' | tr 'A-F' 'a-f'; }

installed_path=$(adb shell pm path "$PKG" | tr -d '\r' | sed -n 's/^package://p' | head -1)
installed=$(adb shell sha256sum "$installed_path" | awk '{print $1}')
name=$(field file)
on_disk=$(adb shell run-as "$PKG" sha256sum "cache/give/$name" | awk '{print $1}')
# build-tools label it "Signer #1", "V2 Signer:" or "Signer (minSdkVersion=…)"; print what we
# got so a format change is easy to see.
apksigner_out=$("$ANDROID_HOME"/build-tools/$(ls "$ANDROID_HOME"/build-tools | sort -V | tail -1)/apksigner verify --print-certs "$APK" 2>/dev/null)
echo "$apksigner_out" | grep -i "sha-256" || true
signer=$(echo "$apksigner_out" | sed -n 's/^.*[Ss]igner.*certificate SHA-256 digest: //p' | head -1 | norm)

echo "installed  $installed ($installed_path)"
echo "plugin     $(field apk)"
echo "copy       $(field copy)"
echo "on disk    $on_disk (cache/give/$name)"
echo "provider   $(field provider) ($(field type))"
echo "cert       $(field cert)"
echo "apksigner  $signer"

[ -n "$installed" ] || fail "couldn't hash the installed APK"
[[ "$name" == Ward-*.apk ]] || fail "unexpected file name $name"
[ "$(field split)" = "false" ] || fail "the emulator install is split"
[ "$(field apk)" = "$installed" ] || fail "plugin hash differs from the installed APK"
[ "$(field copy)" = "$installed" ] || fail "copy hash differs from the installed APK"
[ "$on_disk" = "$installed" ] || fail "copy on disk differs from the installed APK"
[ "$(field provider)" = "$installed" ] || fail "copy read through the FileProvider differs"
[ "$(field type)" = "application/vnd.android.package-archive" ] || fail "FileProvider gives type $(field type)"
[ -n "$signer" ] && [ "$(field cert | norm)" = "$signer" ] || fail "certificate fingerprint differs from apksigner's"

# The friend's phone: the copy, and only the copy, installs and opens.
adb exec-out run-as "$PKG" cat "cache/give/$name" > friend.apk
[ "$(sha256sum friend.apk | awk '{print $1}')" = "$installed" ] || fail "pulled copy differs"
adb uninstall "$PKG"
adb install friend.apk
adb logcat -c
adb shell am start -W -n "$PKG/.MainActivity"
sleep 8
adb logcat -d > give-logcat.txt
adb shell pidof "$PKG" > /dev/null || fail "the friend's copy didn't stay open"
! grep -E "FATAL EXCEPTION.*org\.ward\.app|AndroidRuntime.*org\.ward\.app" give-logcat.txt || fail "the friend's copy crashed"
echo "give-check: the copy matches the installed APK and installs on a fresh phone"

Ward

A guardian that lives on a child's own device. It spots cyberbullying in English, Roman Urdu,
Hinglish and Bangla, keeps the evidence, coaches the next step, and trains kids to bounce back.
Open-weight Gemma, running locally. No server and no account: a child's messages never go to us or to any AI company.

No release yet. Until the first version is published, build Ward from source.

The bully is the ghost haunting the chat. Ward is the ghost on your side. Before you put Ward in front of a child, read the draft [safeguarding policy](docs/SAFEGUARDING.md): what Ward will never do, what hasn't been reviewed by a child-protection professional yet, and [how to raise a concern](docs/SAFEGUARDING.md#10-raising-a-concern-about-the-project-itself). ## What this is, and what it isn't Ward is a response to World Solve problem [WS05937](https://www.worldsolve.org/index.php?view=problem&id=5937): *Building effective interventions for cyberbullying harming children by 2030*, built for the DEV Hacktoberfest pnpm install node apps/web/scripts/copy-ort.mjs # Ward Lite's offline runtime (not in git); rerun after updating packages ollama pull gemma4:e4b # the close read; Ward still works without it pnpm dev # http://localhost:5199 pnpm test # every package, plus the viewer, corrections and red-team leak check pnpm eval # the scorecard (also needs: ollama pull shieldgemma:2b) ``` Skip the `copy-ort` step and the app still runs, but without Ward Lite, in the dev server and in every build below: where Gemma isn't set up, Ward reads with the word lists alone. - **Desktop:** `pnpm --filter @ward/desktop start`. No Ollama? Me → "Gemma inside Ward" downloads Gemma 4 once (4.6 GB) and runs it through llama.cpp inside the app. `--lab` (or the switch in Me) makes Ward forget everything on close, for shared school computers. `pnpm --filter @ward/desktop dist` builds an installer for your own computer into `release/`. GitHub Actions (`desktop.yml`) builds and launch-tests installers for macOS, Windows and Linux when run by hand; none has been published as a release yet. - **Android:** `mobile/` is a Capacitor shell with the app bundled inside and a small native plugin for Share to Ward. `pnpm --filter @ward/web build && pnpm --filter @ward/mobile apk` builds a debug APK (needs the Android SDK and JDK 21). `android.yml` builds it and launch-tests it on an emulator with Wi-Fi off. Cloud backup is off, so the vault never leaves the phone. - **Phone + family computer:** start Ollama on the computer with `OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0`, then put `http://:11434` in Ward's Me screen on the phone. The phone then sends the chats it checks to that computer over your home network, unencrypted, so only do this on a network you trust. `OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0` lets anyone on that network use the computer's Ollama: never set it on school or public Wi-Fi. ### Opening an unsigned build Ward's installers aren't signed yet, so the first time you open one your computer warns you. - **macOS 15 and later:** open Ward once and click Done on the warning. Then open System Settings → Privacy & Security, scroll down to Security, and click **Open Anyway** next to the line about Ward. Confirm with your password, and Ward opens. # The Android app (mobile/): the web build bundled inside a Capacitor shell, so Ward works with
# the internet off. Two APKs (mobile/android/app/build.gradle):
#   Ward-android.apk        "lite", the default: no native code, installs on any phone, 32-bit too
#   Ward-android-gemma.apk  adds on-phone Gemma 4 E2B (LiteRT-LM), arm64 phones only
# Run by hand from the Actions tab (APKs kept 14 days). release.yml calls this on a v* tag and
# publishes the APKs; the names never change.
#
# Signing: the keystore lives only in repository secrets (ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64,
# ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD, ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS, ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD; docs/RELEASING.md). Without
# them a hand run builds debug APKs instead (app id org.ward.app.debug, so they install beside a
# release rather than over it), and a release run fails.
name: Android app

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      release:
        description: Build signed release APKs, versioned from the tag
        type: boolean
        default: false

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4.4.0
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@fc06bc1257f339d1d5d8b3a19a8cae5388b55320 # v4.4.0
      - uses: actions/setup-node@49933ea5288caeca8642d1e84afbd3f7d6820020 # v4.4.0
        with:
          node-version: 24
          cache: pnpm
      - uses: actions/setup-java@cf277c60eb25467037889841efdb72551f06f6c3 # v4.9.1
        with:
          distribution: temurin
          java-version: 21
          cache: gradle
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      - run: pnpm --filter @ward/web build
      - run: pnpm sync
        working-directory: mobile
      - name: Keystore
        id: keystore
        env:
          KEYSTORE: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64 }}
          RELEASE: ${{ inputs.release }}
        run: |
          if [ -n "$KEYSTORE" ]; then
            echo "$KEYSTORE" | base64 -d > "$RUNNER_TEMP/ward.p12"
            echo "path=$RUNNER_TEMP/ward.p12" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          elif [ "$RELEASE" = true ]; then
            echo "::error::A release needs the signing secrets (ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64 and the rest, docs/RELEASING.md)."
            exit 1
          else
            echo "::warning::No signing secrets, so these are debug builds."
          fi
      - name: Build
        working-directory: mobile/android
        env:
          WARD_KEYSTORE: ${{ steps.keystore.outputs.path }}
          WARD_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD }}
          WARD_KEY_ALIAS: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS }}
          WARD_KEY_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD }}
          # The tag (v0.1.0) sets versionName and versionCode; a hand run is 0.0.0-dev.
          WARD_VERSION: ${{ github.ref_type == 'tag' && github.ref_name || '' }}
        run: |
          mkdir -p ../../release
          if [ -n "$WARD_KEYSTORE" ]; then type=release; else type=debug; fi
          ./gradlew --no-daemon assembleLite${type^} assembleGemma${type^}
          cp app/build/outputs/apk/lite/$type/app-lite-$type.apk ../../release/Ward-android.apk
          cp app/build/outputs/apk/gemma/$type/app-gemma-$type.apk ../../release/Ward-android-gemma.apk
          tools="$ANDROID_HOME/build-tools/$(ls "$ANDROID_HOME"/build-tools | sort -V | tail -1)"
          for apk in ../../release/*.apk; do
            echo "== $(basename "$apk"): $("$tools"/aapt2 dump badging "$apk" | head -1)"
            "$tools"/apksigner verify --print-certs "$apk" | grep -i "SHA-256"
          done
      # Lite must have no native code at all: that is what lets it install on 32-bit and any other
      # ABI. Gemma carries LiteRT-LM's libraries for arm64 and nothing else.
      - name: Native libraries
        run: |
          for apk in Ward-android Ward-android-gemma; do
            unzip -l release/$apk.apk | awk '{ print $4 }' | grep '^lib/' | sort > $apk-libs.txt || true
            echo "== $apk.apk native libraries:"; cat $apk-libs.txt
          done
          [ ! -s Ward-android-libs.txt ] || { echo "::error::The lite APK has native libraries, so it won't install on every phone"; exit 1; }
          diff -u - Ward-android-gemma-libs.txt <<'EOF' || { echo "::error::The gemma APK's native libraries changed (expected above, got below)"; exit 1; }
          lib/arm64-v8a/liblitertlm_jni.so
          EOF
      # Ward Lite reads on the phone only if ONNX Runtime's wasm and the model are in the APK;
      # without them Ward quietly falls back to word lists alone.
      - name: Ward Lite is in both APKs
        run: |
          for apk in release/*.apk; do
            unzip -l "$apk" | awk '$1 > 0 { print $4 }' > apk-files.txt
            for f in ort/ort-wasm-simd-threaded.asyncify.wasm ort/ort-wasm-simd-threaded.asyncify.mjs models/ward-lite/ward-lite.json models/ward-lite/config.json models/ward-lite/tokenizer.json models/ward-lite/tokenizer_config.json models/ward-lite/onnx/model_quantized.onnx; do
              grep -qxF "assets/public/$f" apk-files.txt || { echo "::error::$f is missing from $apk"; exit 1; }
            done
          done
          echo "Ward Lite: runtime and model are in both APKs"
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@ea165f8d65b6e75b540449e92b4886f43607fa02 # v4.6.2
        with:
          name: ward-android
          path: release/*.apk
          retention-days: 14
      # The emulator's "Give Ward to a friend" check needs a debug build: only it has the check
      # receiver. A run without signing secrets has just built one, so this costs nothing there.
      - name: Debug build for the give-a-friend check
        working-directory: mobile/android
        run: |
          [ -f app/build/outputs/apk/lite/debug/app-lite-debug.apk ] || ./gradlew --no-daemon assembleLiteDebug
          mkdir -p ../../give && cp app/build/outputs/apk/lite/debug/app-lite-debug.apk ../../give/Ward-debug.apk
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@ea165f8d65b6e75b540449e92b4886f43607fa02 # v4.6.2
        with:
          name: ward-android-debug
          path: give/Ward-debug.apk
          retention-days: 3

  # Install the lite APK on an emulator, open it, and keep a screenshot and the log: Ward starts,
  # shows onboarding from the bundle with no network, and doesn't crash. Then "Give Ward to a
  # friend": the copy it shares is exactly the installed APK and installs on a wiped phone.
  # (The emulator is x86_64, so the arm64-only gemma APK can't be launched here.)
  launch:
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@11d5960a326750d5838078e36cf38b85af677262 # v4.4.0
        with:
          sparse-checkout: |
            packages/engine/fixtures
            mobile/ci
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@d3f86a106a0bac45b974a628896c90dbdf5c8093 # v4.3.0
        with:
          name: ward-android
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@d3f86a106a0bac45b974a628896c90dbdf5c8093 # v4.3.0
        with:
          name: ward-android-debug
      - name: Enable KVM
        run: |
          echo 'KERNEL=="kvm", GROUP="kvm", MODE="0666", OPTIONS+="static_node=kvm"' | sudo tee /etc/udev/rules.d/99-kvm4all.rules
          sudo udevadm control --reload-rules
          sudo udevadm trigger --name-match=kvm
      - uses: reactivecircus/android-emulator-runner@a421e43855164a8197daf9d8d40fe71c6996bb0d # v2.38.0
        with:
          api-level: 34
          arch: x86_64
          target: google_apis
          emulator-options: -no-window -gpu swiftshader_indirect -no-snapshot -noaudio -no-boot-anim
          disable-animations: true
          script: |
            bash mobile/ci/launch-check.sh Ward-android.apk
            bash mobile/ci/give-check.sh Ward-debug.apk
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@ea165f8d65b6e75b540449e92b4886f43607fa02 # v4.6.2
        if: always()
        with:
          name: ward-android-launch
          path: |
            launch.png
            share.png
            logcat.txt
            give-logcat.txt
          retention-days: 14

# A release, from a v* tag the owner pushes (docs/RELEASING.md). Builds the signed Android APKs
# (android.yml, including the emulator launch test) and the desktop installers (desktop.yml,
# each launch-tested), then publishes them as a GitHub prerelease with SHA256SUMS and the
# signing certificate's SHA-256 in the release notes: the fingerprint Ward shows under "Give
# Ward to a friend". Fails before building anything if a signing secret is missing.
name: Release

on:
  push:
    tags: ["v*"]

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Signing secrets
        env:
          ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64 }}
          ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD }}
          ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS }}
          ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD }}
        run: |
          missing=""
          for s in ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64 ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD; do
            [ -n "${!s}" ] || missing="$missing $s"
          done
          if [ -n "$missing" ]; then
            echo "::error::Can't release without the signing secrets. Missing:$missing. Add them with gh secret set (docs/RELEASING.md), then delete and push the tag again."
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "All four signing secrets are set."
      - name: Tag is a version
        run: |
          [[ "$GITHUB_REF_NAME" =~ ^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+(-[0-9A-Za-z.-]+)?$ ]] || {
            echo "::error::The tag $GITHUB_REF_NAME isn't a version like v0.1.0 or v0.1.0-rc.1"; exit 1; }

  android:
    needs: check
    uses: ./.github/workflows/android.yml
    with:
      release: true
    secrets: inherit

  desktop:
    needs: check

input.content:
# Releasing Ward

This is for the owner, who holds Ward's Android signing key. CI builds and publishes a release,
but only after you've done steps 1 to 3 once, and only when you push a tag (step 5).

## What a release is

Pushing a tag like `v0.1.0` runs [`release.yml`](../.github/workflows/release.yml):

1. It stops straight away, naming what's missing, if any of the four signing secrets isn't set or
   the tag isn't a version.
2. [`android.yml`](../.github/workflows/android.yml) builds two signed release APKs and launches
   the lite one on an emulator with Wi-Fi off:
   - `Ward-android.apk`, the default "lite" flavour. It has no native code, so it installs on any
     Android 7+ phone, 32-bit Android Go phones included.
   - `Ward-android-gemma.apk`, which adds on-phone Gemma 4 E2B (LiteRT-LM). Its native library is
     arm64 only, so it installs only on 64-bit phones.

   CI checks each APK's native-library list, that Ward Lite's runtime and model are inside both,
   that neither is debug-signed, and that both have the tag's version and the same certificate.
3. [`desktop.yml`](../.github/workflows/desktop.yml) builds and launch-tests the macOS (Apple
   Silicon and Intel), Windows and Linux installers. They aren't code-signed yet.
4. It publishes a GitHub **prerelease** with all six files, a `SHA256SUMS` file, and the signing
   certificate's SHA-256 in the release notes, grouped in fours the way Ward shows it under
   "Give Ward to a friend".

Versions come from the tag. `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` gives Android `versionName` MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH
and `versionCode` MAJOR × 10000 + MINOR × 100 + PATCH, so `v0.1.0` is 100 and each tag must be
higher than the last. MINOR and PATCH must stay under 100. A suffix such as `v0.1.0-rc.1` is kept
in the name but shares the code with `v0.1.0`. The desktop apps take the same version. A build
from anything but a tag is `0.0.0-dev`.

Debug builds are a separate app, `org.ward.app.debug`, so trying one never means uninstalling a
release (which would wipe the child's vault, since cloud backup is off).

## Before the first release

- Ward Lite works in a CI-built APK on a real phone: run "Android app" by hand from the Actions
  tab, install `Ward-android.apk` from the run's artifacts, and check a chat with the internet off.
- The lite APK installs and runs on a real 32-bit phone, ideally an Android Go phone with 2 to
  3 GB of RAM. CI can't test this: its emulator is 64-bit.
- CI is green on `main`.

## 1. Create the signing key (once, ever)

Do this on your own computer, in a folder that isn't synced to iCloud, Google Drive or Dropbox
(on a Mac, Desktop and Documents often are). You need `keytool`, which comes with any JDK 21.

```bash
mkdir -p ~/ward-signing && cd ~/ward-signing
openssl rand -base64 24   # the keystore password: save it in your password manager now
keytool -genkeypair -v -storetype PKCS12 -keystore ward-release.p12 -alias ward \
  -keyalg RSA -keysize 4096 -validity 10000 -dname "CN=Ward, O=Ward"
```

`keytool` asks for the password twice: paste the one you generated. A PKCS12 keystore uses the
same password for the key, so `ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD` below is that same password.

Write down the certificate's SHA-256. Every genuine Ward APK will carry exactly this fingerprint:

```bash
keytool -list -v -keystore ward-release.p12 -alias ward | grep SHA256
```

## 2. Back it up twice, offline

If the key is lost, no future Ward can update the copies already on children's phones: they
would have to uninstall, and that deletes the vault. If it leaks, anyone can sign a fake Ward that
passes the fingerprint check. So:

- Copy `ward-release.p12` to **two** encrypted USB drives (on a Mac, format them as APFS
  (Encrypted) in Disk Utility). Keep them in two different buildings, never with the laptop.
- Keep the password apart from the drives: in your password manager and on paper in a sealed
  envelope with one of them.
- Check each backup really works:

  ```bash
  shasum -a 256 ~/ward-signing/ward-release.p12 /Volumes/<drive>/ward-release.p12
  keytool -list -keystore /Volumes/<drive>/ward-release.p12 -alias ward
  ```

- Name a second custodian who knows where one drive and the envelope are.
- Never commit the keystore (`.gitignore` blocks `*.p12`, `*.jks` and `*.keystore`), email it, or
  put it in a chat.

## 3. Add the four secrets

With the [GitHub CLI](https://cli.github.com) logged in as the repository owner:

```bash
cd ~/ward-signing
base64 -i ward-release.p12 | gh secret set ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64 --repo MuhammadMurtuzaHussain/ward
gh secret set ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD --repo MuhammadMurtuzaHussain/ward   # paste the password when asked
gh secret set ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS --repo MuhammadMurtuzaHussain/ward --body ward
gh secret set ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD --repo MuhammadMurtuzaHussain/ward        # the same password again
gh secret list --repo MuhammadMurtuzaHussain/ward                            # all four should be listed
```

Once both backups are checked, delete the working copy: `rm -P ~/ward-signing/ward-release.p12`.

## 4. Try a signed build (no release)

Run the Android workflow by hand. With the secrets set it now builds release-signed APKs,
versioned `0.0.0-dev`:

```bash
gh workflow run android.yml --repo MuhammadMurtuzaHussain/ward --ref main
gh run watch --repo MuhammadMurtuzaHussain/ward $(gh run list --repo MuhammadMurtuzaHussain/ward --workflow android.yml --limit 1 --json databaseId -q '.[0].databaseId')
```

The "Build" step prints each APK's certificate SHA-256: it must match the one from step 1. You can
install this APK on a test phone; the tagged release will update it in place.

## 5. Tag the release

```bash
git switch main && git pull
git tag -a v0.1.0 -m "Ward 0.1.0 (preview)"
git push origin v0.1.0
gh run watch --repo MuhammadMurtuzaHussain/ward $(gh run list --repo MuhammadMurtuzaHussain/ward --workflow release.yml --limit 1 --json databaseId -q '.[0].databaseId')
```

If the run fails before publishing, fix the cause on `main`, then move the tag and push it again:

```bash
git push --delete origin v0.1.0 && git tag -d v0.1.0
git tag -a v0.1.0 -m "Ward 0.1.0 (preview)" && git push origin v0.1.0
```

Once a release is published, never move its tag: fix forward with `v0.1.1`.

## 6. After it's published

- The release page has six files plus `SHA256SUMS`, and the fingerprint in the notes is the one
  from step 1.
- Install `Ward-android.apk` on a phone from the release page. Me → Give Ward to a friend shows
  the same fingerprint boxes.
- A prerelease is never GitHub's "latest" release, so `releases/latest` links don't find it.
  The README's commented-out download badges and the "Give Ward" QR code
  (`apps/web/src/lib/giveWard.ts`) use `releases/latest`: point them at `releases` (or this tag)
  while every release is a prerelease, or publish a release that isn't marked prerelease.
- Then replace the README's "No release yet" line with the download badges.

## Not done yet

- The desktop installers aren't signed (macOS Developer ID, Windows via SignPath). The README
  explains how to open them anyway.
- No Google Play listing. If Ward goes on Play, choose "use my own key" when enrolling in Play
  App Signing, so this same key stays Ward's identity; that choice can't be undone.

I pushed four commits to main: `c715d1e`, `72fb13b`, `5452eec` and `0c87194`. The Android and desktop workflows, run by hand on main, both passed. So did CI and Pages on that push.

**What changed**
- **Two Android APKs.**
  - `Ward-android.apk` is the default "lite" build. CI checks it contains no native code at all, so nothing ties it to a chip type.
  - `Ward-android-gemma.apk` is for arm64 phones only. CI checks its only native library is `lib/arm64-v8a/liblitertlm_jni.so`.
  - The Gemma plugin only exists in the gemma build. In the web app, the "Gemma on this phone" card now also checks whether the plugin is present, so it stays hidden in the lite app. That one line in `phoneGemma.ts` is my only change under `apps/web/src`.
  - The emulator test runs on the lite APK and passed, including the "Give Ward to a friend" check.
- **Version numbers.** The app version comes from the git tag: `v0.1.0` becomes versionName 0.1.0, versionCode 100. A build without a tag is `0.0.0-dev`. Debug builds install as a separate app, `org.ward.app.debug`, so trying one never wipes a real install.
- **Release workflow.** Pushing a `v*` tag runs `release.yml`:
  - It stops at once if any of the four signing secrets is missing, and names which ones.
  - It builds the signed APKs and the desktop installers, and runs the same launch tests.
  - It checks the APKs aren't debug-signed, carry the tag's version, and share one certificate.
  - It publishes a **prerelease** with `SHA256SUMS`. The release notes show the certificate's SHA-256 grouped in fours, the same way Ward's Give screen shows it.
- **CI hardening.** Every action in every workflow is pinned to a commit, including the Pages workflow another session added. Dependabot is on for actions and npm, and it has already opened PRs #1 to #4. One of them bumps TypeScript to 7, a major version, so it needs a look before merging.
- **Docs.** The README's macOS 15 and SmartScreen steps were already right from earlier today; I only added the two APKs and a releases line. `docs/RELEASING.md` is new.

**Runs:**
- Android on main: [41231035295](https://github.com/MuhammadMurtuzaHussain/ward/actions/runs/41231035295)
- Desktop on main: [41231037909](https://github.com/MuhammadMurtuzaHussain/ward/actions/runs/41231037909)
- Earlier branch runs: [Android](https://github.com/MuhammadMurtuzaHussain/ward/actions/runs/41230490019), [desktop](https://github.com/MuhammadMurtuzaHussain/ward/actions/runs/41230492259)

**Problems to know about**
- **The prerelease won't fix the 404 links.** GitHub never counts a prerelease as "latest", so `releases/latest` will still 404. That breaks the Give QR code (`giveWard.ts:7`) and the README's commented-out badges. Whoever owns the web app should point them at `/releases`. I left this in a note in the shared folder.
- **Gemma users can pass on an APK that won't install.** "Give Ward to a friend" in the gemma build shares that arm64-only APK. A friend with a 32-bit phone can't install it.
- **The emulator screenshots are empty.** `launch.png` and `share.png` come out at 0 bytes, and were already empty before my changes. The pass/fail checks don't depend on them.
- **Real-phone testing is still open.** Nothing has been tried on a real 32-bit phone yet, and RELEASING.md lists that as a step before the first release.

**What the owner runs to cut v0.1.0** (each step is explained in `docs/RELEASING.md`)

Create the key, then copy it to two encrypted USB drives kept apart, and keep the password separately:
```bash
mkdir -p ~/ward-signing && cd ~/ward-signing && openssl rand -base64 24
```
```bash
keytool -genkeypair -v -storetype PKCS12 -keystore ward-release.p12 -alias ward -keyalg RSA -keysize 4096 -validity 10000 -dname "CN=Ward, O=Ward"
```
Add the four secrets. The key password is the same as the keystore password:
```bash
base64 -i ward-release.p12 | gh secret set ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64 --repo MuhammadMurtuzaHussain/ward
```
```bash
gh secret set ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD --repo MuhammadMurtuzaHussain/ward
```
```bash
gh secret set ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS --repo MuhammadMurtuzaHussain/ward --body ward
```
```bash
gh secret set ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD --repo MuhammadMurtuzaHussain/ward
```
Then tag, from an up-to-date main:
```bash
git tag -a v0.1.0 -m "Ward 0.1.0 (preview)" && git push origin v0.1.0
```
